markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

eventMetadata.context_description: The open 2028 Democratic field remains fragmented in the invisible primary, with no declared candidates or consensus leader nearly two years before the first primaries, driving traders to spread probability across progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and moderates like Gavin Newsom. Recent DNC approval of a revised calendar placing South Carolina first on January 22, 2028, followed by Nevada and other diverse states, has highlighted structural shifts that could reward candidates with strong appeal in those electorates. Jon Ossoff has narrowed gaps through targeted rallies emphasizing economic issues, while polling aggregates show Kamala Harris ahead nationally yet lower in prediction markets. This tight distribution reflects competing visions for party direction and uncertainty over who can consolidate support ahead of formal announcements, fundraising surges, or early-state momentum.
